phrases.meaning_here: price of one currency in another

statements.decisive_phrase: units of a foreign currency ... one unit of home currency

phrases.phrase: units of a foreign currency exchangeable for one unit of home currency

core_fact: Economic Surveys 2022-23/2023-24 describe the Indian economy as resilient amid geopolitical shocks, crediting calibrated fiscal and monetary policies for post-COVID macro-financial stability.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The Indian economy demonstrated resilience despite global geopolitical challenges.

phrases.meaning_here: growth sustained amid war, supply shocks

statements.label: R
statements.text: India's fiscal and monetary policies ensured economic and financial stability post-COVID.

statements.label: R->A
statements.text: R explains A.

reconstruction.correct_statement: Policy-driven stability explains India's resilience.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Survey A-R pairs: resilience <- macro stability, fiscal prudence, RBI tightening.

practice: AI-GENERATED PRACTICE (not an APPSC PYQ): 'RBI raised the repo rate by 250 bps between May 2022 and Feb 2023' - T.

core_fact: RBI Annual Report 2023-24: RBI conducted 49 fine-tuning operations (VRR/VRRR, both injection and absorption) in FY24 to keep liquidity in line with the monetary policy stance.

statements.label: opt1
statements.text: The purpose of the 49 fine-tuning operations was to tighten liquidity conditions.
statements.true_fact: The operations both injected and absorbed liquidity to align with the stance.

statements.label: opt2
statements.text: The purpose of the 49 fine-tuning operations was to ease liquidity conditions.
statements.true_fact: The operations both injected and absorbed liquidity.

statements.label: opt3
statements.text: The purpose of the 49 fine-tuning operations was to maintain liquidity conditions in alignment with the monetary policy stance.
statements.decisive_phrase: alignment with the monetary policy stance

statements.label: opt4
statements.text: The purpose of the 49 fine-tuning operations was to increase the money supply.
statements.true_fact: Fine-tuning manages transient liquidity, not money-supply growth.

reconstruction.correct_statement: Fine-tuning kept liquidity aligned with the policy stance.
reconstruction.decisive: alignment with the monetary policy stance
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Liquidity tools: main 14-day VRR/VRRR, fine-tuning (overnight-13 days), OMO, FX swaps, SDF, MSF.

practice: AI-GENERATED PRACTICE (not an APPSC PYQ): 'Variable rate reverse repo auctions absorb liquidity from banks' - T.

core_fact: RBI announced (10 Aug 2023) an incremental CRR of 10% on the increase in NDTL between 19 May and 28 July 2023 (effective 12 Aug), impounding about Rs 1.1 lakh crore of surplus liquidity (from the Rs 2000 note withdrawal); it was phased out by October 2023.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The RBI announced a temporary I-CRR of 10 per cent on 10 August 2023.
statements.fact_source: RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, 10 Aug 2023

statements.label: B
statements.text: This action impounded about Rs 1.1 lakh crore from the banking system.

reconstruction.correct_statement: I-CRR 10% (Aug 2023) impounded ~Rs 1.1 lakh crore.
reconstruction.decisive: Both statements A and B are correct
reconstruction.why: Temporary absorption of excess liquidity after Rs 2000 note withdrawal.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: I-CRR 2023: 10%, NDTL rise 19 May-28 Jul, ~Rs 1.1 lakh cr, released in phases by Oct 2023; regular CRR then 4.5%.
